writeup.headline: KBR rates Hold: low valuation offsets a heavy debt load, soft growth and middling margins.
writeup.thesis: KBR scores 51, a Hold, because a strong valuation score of 85 is pulled down by weak balance sheet, growth and quality scores. In absolute terms the shares look low at 0.7x sales, 14.3x free cash flow and 9.9x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 2.0 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock is cheap against its own history, for example cheaper than at 53 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S. The balance sheet scores just 14, with net debt at 6.31 times free cash flow and cash covering only 0.12 of debt. Growth scores 39 on a TTM revenue decline of 3.6%, though latest-quarter revenue growth of 1.6% year on year shows growth sped up by 6.3 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is modest at 40, with a 14.5% gross margin, 9.5% operating margin and 4.6% FCF margin, partly helped by diluted share count down 1.6% year on year.
key_risks: High leverage: net debt is 6.31 times free cash flow and cash covers only 0.12 of debt.
Revenue is still down over the trailing year, with a TTM revenue decline of 3.6%, and Q3 revenue slightly missed consensus.
NASA insourcing remains a headwind for the government business.
Thin margins (4.6% FCF margin) leave little room for contract cost overruns.
Shares are down 18.4% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and Citigroup trimmed its price target while consensus sits at Hold.
what_would_change: A drop of 7 points to below 45 would move the rating to Sell, for example if the valuation score fell as the shares rerate or if the balance sheet weakened further.
A gain of 14 points to 65 would be needed for Buy, most plausibly from sustained revenue growth lifting the growth score and debt reduction lifting the balance sheet score.
Continued wins such as the Aramco, NATO and ammonia revamp awards translating into higher margins would support the quality score.
Post-earnings analyst downgrades or a cut to the reaffirmed FY26 outlook would hurt the news and trend scores.
